200.description: The state after the change, including the new `rotation.nextRotationAt`.

enabled.description: Whether encryption is turned on: a key exists that has not been retired. `true` from the moment an operator turns it on, including the grace window before that key activates (`keys[].pendingActivation`); `false` from the moment it is turned off, including the grace window in which the retiring key still protects new writes (`keys[].active`).

keyConfigured.description: Whether this engine process holds the key-encryption key (`ENCRYPTION_KEY`). Without it, encryption cannot be turned on and no key can be added from this process.

keys.description: Every key that has ever protected `onboardings.context`, most recent first.

id.description: The id written into every envelope this key produced.

createdBy.description: The operator who turned encryption on or added this key, as the bearer token identified them, or the unknown-actor marker when admin authentication is off. Null only for a row inserted outside the API; every key the engine creates records who asked for it.

activatedAt.description: When this key becomes (or became) the active one. May be in the future — see `pendingActivation`.

deletedAt.description: When this key stops (or stopped) protecting new writes — superseded by a rotation or retired by turning encryption off; null while it has not been. May be in the future: the key stays `active` until then.

active.description: Whether this is the key `encrypt` currently uses.

pendingActivation.description: Whether this key has been added but has not activated yet — `activatedAt` is still in the future, during the grace window that gives every replica a chance to learn of it before anything encrypts with it. The previous key remains `active` until then.

interval.description: How often the engine rotates the key on its own; `null` when it does not, and while encryption is off.

allOf.description: How often the engine rotates the encryption key on its own, measured from the active key's creation: 48 or 96 hours, one or two weeks, or a fixed 30-day month.
allOf.title: EncryptionKeyRotationInterval

nextRotationAt.description: When the next automatic rotation falls due: the active key's `createdAt` plus `interval`. Null whenever `interval` is. In the past for a schedule that has come due but whose rotation the engine has not run yet — it checks every `ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`.

pending.description: Onboardings not yet in the chosen state: stored as plain JSON while encryption is on, still encrypted while it is off. A row on a superseded key is not pending — rotation is lazy, so it moves to the current key the next time it is written.

reencrypting.description: Whether an operator's request to re-encrypt every stored onboarding onto the active key is still outstanding. While it is, `progress.pending` counts rows on a superseded key as work; otherwise those rows are not pending, because rotation is lazy.

400.description: The body or query violates its declared shape; `message` names each violated rule.

schema.description: NestJS's default error envelope, returned where the framework answers instead of the engine: request validation (`400`, `message` lists each violated rule), the admin bearer guard (`401`, `403`, `503`), and a `500` on the submit and provider-callback routes where a connector adapter fails with a plain error rather than a coded refusal.
schema.title: NestHttpError
